contract_plain_english: For the constant-coefficient real linear system q_t + A q_x = 0, hyperbolicity means that A has real eigenvalues and a complete eigenvector basis (printed pp. 1 and 3). With constant left and right initial states separated at x = 0 as in (1.11), the source asserts that the Riemann problem can be solved using the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of A, referring the construction to Chapter 3 (printed pp. 5–6). The surrounding text describes hyperbolic Riemann solutions as typically depending on x/t and comprising finitely many waves with constant propagation speeds (printed p. 5); the eigenvalues give the linear wave speeds (printed p. 3). The supplied passage leaves the interface values, precise discontinuous-solution formulation, and detailed spectral construction unspecified (printed p. 5, opening paragraph and section 1.2.1; printed p. 6, continuation).
